messages:
maya: Heads-up — posted an RFC for extracting our monolithic config/secrets + rollout logic into a dedicated 'config-store' service. goal: reduce cross-cutting tech debt, make private deployments simpler, enable tenant-scoped overrides.

sam: reading now. quick q: is this mostly about secrets or all runtime config? :thinking_face:

maya: both. two main pieces: 1) runtime config (batch sizes, quant profiles, routing weights) that's currently in the orchestration DB, 2) secrets/kms pointers used by Private and Dedicated. they live in the same codepaths which causes a lot of accidental coupling.

jin: big 👍 on separation. we've hit so many race conditions when orch reloads configs during rollouts. how do you handle consistency? distributed cache invalidation is tricky.

maya: agreed. plan is: config-store exposes versioned read APIs + a light notification stream for cache invalidation (pubsub webhook or consumer). we keep eventual consistency but provide a single-tenant strong-read endpoint for critical secrets.

aleks: can you paste the proposed API shape? would like to see how clients look.

maya: sure — from the RFC:

```
GET /v1/tenants/{t}/configs?key=redwood.runtime.batch
Response: {"value":"64","version":"v2026-03-01-1"}

POST /v1/tenants/{t}/secrets
Body: {"name":"s3-creds","kms_ref":"projects/.../keys/abcd"}
Response: {"id":"secret-123","created_at":"..."}
```

sam: ok, so config-store becomes the single source of truth. migration headache: we have thousands of ad-hoc keys in orch DB and a few inline secrets in repo — how to migrate safely?

maya: migration plan in the RFC:
- import + normalize keys into config-store with original metadata
- create compatibility proxy in orchestration: reads forwarded to config-store but writes still land in orch DB
- run in read-only mode for a month, surface diffs to owners
- flip writes to config-store once owners sign off

priya: what about latency? ornch is hot path for inference decisions. extra hop could add ~2-4ms p99 if we call config-store synchronously.

maya: good point. patterns:
- prefer local cache with TTL + versioned invalidation
- critical reads (secrets for initialization) use direct strong-read
- policy decisions that require <1ms will keep decision caches in-process and refresh asynchronously

jin: monitoring and runbook? if config-store is down, we need graceful fallback to last-known values.

maya: yes. propose: clients fallback to cached version + fire alerts. the console will show config-store health per-region/tenant. we add synthetic checks for key reads.

aleks: compatibility and auth: how do existing tokens / service accounts authenticate? we must not break Private deployments that expect customer-managed KMS.

maya: auth will be pluggable. default is mTLS + short-lived tokens for hosted. for Private, we provide an on-prem sidecar + service account mapping to local KMS. RFC has sequence diagrams.

sam: rollout strategy sounds reasonable. estimate of engineering work? rough timeline?

maya: MVP (read-only + cache + notification webhook) — 6w. full migration tooling + secret CR/rotation flows — +4w. cross-team migration coordination will be biggest blocker.

priya: one more ops ask — include per-tenant audit logs and retention controls in the initial MVP. we need to comply with SOC/GDPR requests.

maya: added to the checklist. also adding a small CLI to audit owner mappings and diff configs.

deploy-bot: deployment scheduled: config-store/mvp -> staging on 1772008123 by maya

jin: thanks — I'll pair on the caching and invalidation tests. happy to own test harness for race conditions.

maya: awesome. will post the RFC link and detailed migration playbook in #eng-oncall and schedule a sync with platform + security next week. :calendar:
thread_text: Extracting config/secrets into a dedicated service to reduce coupling and simplify private deployments. Includes versioned reads, notification stream, migration proxy, per-tenant audit and pluggable auth.
